# Sheet Table

**Figma:** Table/Sheet/Cell, .Primitives/Table/Sheet/Code, .Primitives/Table/Sheet/Key over Table/Cell/Header (page ❖ Table 1595:2631, doc frame 17100:7996)  
**Import:** `import { SheetTable, SheetCode, SheetKeys, SheetKey, TableText } from "@zen-ds/react";`

Reference rows whose text runs long, read in full: props and their types, API signatures, keyboard shortcuts, token values.

## Use it for
- A props or API reference: names, type unions and descriptions that wrap.
- Keyboard shortcuts: SheetKeys chips beside what each one does.
- Token or setting references whose values and notes run to several lines.

## Use something else for
- Records people scan, sort, select or open → Table (one-line rows at Table/Cell/Size).
- One or two attributes per item → List Item.
- Key/value details of one record → Description List.
- Paragraphs of prose → Text in the page; a sheet holds rows.

## Figma → React
| Figma | Prop | Values / notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Columns | `columns[] {id, header, width, cell}` | One column each; give the name and value columns a width ("18%", "160px") and leave the long one without, so it takes the rest (Figma FILL). |
| Rows | `rows · getRowId` | One row per item; getRowId when rows have no id. |
| Content | `SheetCode · SheetKeys · SheetKey · TableText` | Figma Table/Sheet/Cell's Content slot: code (a prop, a type, a signature) in Body/Code/Regular, a shortcut as Key chips ("Shift + Tab / Tab"), words in a Text-Cell (bold for the row's name). All of it wraps. |
| Width | `minWidth` | Below this width the sheet scrolls sideways instead of squeezing its columns (680px for four columns of code). |
| Empty | `empty` | A full-width row when rows is empty. |

## Props
Generated from the TypeScript source; full JSON in `docs/api/sheet-table.json`.

### SheetTable
Figma Table/Sheet (page ❖ Table, doc frame 17100:7996; cell set Table/Sheet/Cell 17100:8027): reference rows whose text runs long — props and their types, API signatures, keyboard shortcuts, token values. Each row grows with its content from a Table/Cell/Size minimum, aligned to the top, so every line is read; a Table keeps one-line rows and cuts long text (user rule 2026-10-13). Header: Table/Cell/Header (Table/Header/Size, All-Caps/S, Content/Neutral/ Light). Cells: Spacing/Padding/Small × Medium, Table-Cell/Background/Default, a 1px Border/Neutral/Pale rule under every row but the last (Divider=No). Static: no sorting, selection or row clicks — those rows belong in a Table.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` | — | The root element (the scroll box around the `<table>`). |
| `columns` (required) | `SheetTableColumn<T>[]` | — |  |
| `rows` (required) | _HTML attribute_ | — | The items, one row each. |
| `getRowId` | `(row: T, index: number) => string` | `(row, index) => rowIdOf(row, index)` | A stable, unique id per row (React keys). Default: the row's `id` field, else its position. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | — | Names the sheet for screen readers when there is no visible `caption` (or use `aria-labelledby`). |
| `caption` | `ReactNode` | — | Visible caption above the sheet (Heading/4), which also names it. |
| `minWidth` | `string` | — | The narrowest the columns may get, a CSS length (e.g. "680px"): a narrower container scrolls the sheet sideways instead of squeezing its columns into a word per line. Leave it unset for two short columns. |
| `empty` | `ReactNode` | — | Rendered in a full-width row when `rows` is empty (e.g. "No keyboard shortcuts"). |
| `className` | `string` | — |  |

### SheetCode
Figma .Primitives/Table/Sheet/Code (17100:8013): a code value in a SheetTable cell — a prop name, a type union, a signature, a default. Body/Code/Regular in Content/Neutral/Strongest; it wraps, never cuts.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` | — | Forwarded to the root `<code>` element. |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` | — | The code, as plain text. |

### SheetKey
Figma .Primitives/Table/Sheet/Key (17100:8015): one keyboard key (Tab, Shift, →, Esc) as a chip — Element-Size/Popular/ Base minimum, Spacing/Padding/2XSmall sides, Corner-Radius/2XSmall, Background/Neutral/Pale with a Border/Neutral/Pale ring and a 2px foot, Body/Code/Regular in Content/Neutral/Strongest.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` | — | Forwarded to the root `<kbd>` element. |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` | — | The key's name, as printed on it ("Shift", "Tab", "→"). |

### SheetKeys
A shortcut written as text — "Shift + Tab / Tab", "G then I" — as SheetKey chips with their separators between them: Spacing/Gap/2XSmall apart, the separators in Body/Small/Regular, Content/Neutral/Light (Figma Table/Sheet Keyboard example). `+` joins keys pressed together, `/` separates alternatives, `then` a sequence.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLSpanElement>` | — | Forwarded to the root `<span>` element. |
| `value` (required) | `string` | — | The shortcut: keys joined by " + ", " / " or " then ". |

### Types
Object shapes the props above refer to.

```ts
interface SheetTableColumn<T> { id: string; header: ReactNode; width?: string; cell?: (row: T, index: number) => ReactNode; content?: SheetTableContent; field?: string; bold?: boolean; }
type SheetTableContent = "text" | "code" | "keys"
```

## ✅ Do
- Name the sheet (aria-labelledby pointing at its section heading, a caption, or aria-label; harness: sheet-table/needs-name).
- Write code values with SheetCode and shortcuts with SheetKeys, so a type or a key reads as code, not prose.
- Give a sheet with several code columns a minWidth (about 680px for four), so a phone scrolls it sideways instead of breaking every word.

## ❌ Don't
- Don't use a SheetTable for data people act on: it has no sorting, selection or row clicks; that is a Table.
- Don't cut long text in a reference with a Table's ellipsis: the reader needs the whole type or description.
- Don't write keys as plain text ("Shift+Tab"): SheetKeys draws each key as a chip.

## Accessibility
- Native table semantics: th scope=col for every header; the wrapper scrolls horizontally on small screens.
- Keys are kbd elements; the separators (+, /, then) are read between them.

## Content
- Headers are short nouns (Prop, Type, Default, Description; Key, Action).
- A description is one or two sentences: what the value does and when to use it.

## Harness (`npm run usage:check`)
| Rule | Severity | Checks | Suppress with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sheet-table/needs-name` | error | A SheetTable is named by a caption, aria-label or aria-labelledby (its section heading). | `zen-allow-table-name: <reason>` |
| `table/reference-in-sheet` | warn | Reference rows — code values, type unions, keyboard shortcuts — belong in a SheetTable: a Table's rows stay one line at Table/Cell/Size and cut them with an ellipsis (user rule 2026-10-13). | `zen-allow-table-reference: <reason>` |
| `interaction/no-noop-handler` | warn | Every interaction a Zen control offers works: no no-op handlers (`() => {}`, `() => undefined`), which leave a field that ignores typing and ↑/↓ or a Dismiss that stays. Chat has chat/no-locked-interaction. | `zen-allow-noop-handler: <reason>` |
